title: DT Guardian
description: DT Guardian: a simulated, offline-first edge controller for a 200 kVA distribution transformer. In a simulated 6-hour outage it cut unserved essential energy from 121.2 to 56.7 kWh.
lede: A simulated, offline-first edge controller for a 200 kVA distribution transformer. An IS 2026-7 thermal model drives MILP dispatch of battery storage, EV charging and pump loads, with a fail-safe fallback when the forecast or solver fails.

blocks.text: Schneider Electric Yuva Yodha Energy Tech Hackathon, Challenge 3 (grid reliability and renewable intermittency), prototype round. The project aims to turn a distribution transformer's thermal headroom into neighbourhood flexibility: EV and pump demand shifts toward renewable-rich hours, and critical loads stay on during supply gaps.
The prototype is a Python simulator with a thermal twin, a load forecaster, a rolling-horizon dispatcher, baselines and an experiment pipeline. It is an offline-first edge controller.

forecast or solver fails ──▶ fail-safe fallback
blocks.caption: A conformal load forecast and the IS 2026-7 thermal model feed a MILP dispatcher, which schedules battery storage, EV charging and pump loads. If the forecast or the solver fails, a fail-safe fallback takes over.

blocks.text: All results are simulated. Neighbourhood loads and control experiments are synthetic; the weather input is real Lucknow reanalysis data.

items: No field deployment and no utility integration. This is a prototype-round entry.
The electrical model uses a voltage proxy. OpenDSS integration and the dashboard are unfinished.
The outage result covers a simulated 6-hour, battery-stressed outage only.
